tagline: Clarify a managed data workflow before provisioning it.
introduction: A data-platform companion for Aiven documentation, helping map requirements, review integration assumptions and plan observable operations.
welcome: What would you like to understand or plan with Aiven? Choose a starter below, or share a small redacted example.

capabilities.title: Map data requirements
capabilities.description: Relate an application workload to the appropriate Aiven documentation areas.

capabilities.title: Review integration assumptions
capabilities.description: Inspect a proposed data flow for identity, schema and failure gaps.

capabilities.title: Plan operational evidence
capabilities.description: Define the evidence needed to support a reliability claim.

starterPrompts: Help map a small event app's transactional and event-stream needs to Aiven documentation.
Review this proposed Aiven data flow for source-of-truth, retry and schema-evolution problems.
What should I measure before claiming this managed data pipeline is reliable?

sources.title: Aiven documentation
sources.summary: Official managed data services, platform, developer tools and integration documentation.

sources.title: Identify PostgreSQL slow queries
sources.summary: pg_stat_statements supports slow-query investigation; column names vary by PostgreSQL version. Query-plan inspection is a next step, not proof that a particular index helps.

sources.title: Repair PostgreSQL indexes
sources.summary: REINDEX addresses index corruption and can apply locks that interfere with normal database use; this is not general index-selection evidence.

sources.title: Monitor Kafka consumer groups
sources.summary: Extra consumers beyond partition count remain idle. Consumer group replication lag is the per-partition high-watermark minus group offset; lag requires investigation, not a single assumed cause.
